title: BE STRONG AND COURAGEOUS
text: Haven’t I commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid. Don’t be dismayed, for Yahweh your God is with you wherever you go.

reflection.kids: God told Joshua to be brave. Not because the job was small — because God was going with him.
reflection.teens: This is a command, not a pep talk. Courage is something Joshua is told to choose, and the reason given is a person, not a plan.

prayer.kids: God, help me be brave today, because you are with me.
prayer.teens: God, I am not always brave. Go with me into the thing I would rather avoid.

challenge.kids: Do one thing today that feels a bit scary but is good.
challenge.teens: Do the thing you have been putting off because it is uncomfortable.

devotion.kids: Joshua was taking over from Moses — an impossible act to follow. Four times God tells him to be strong. Every time, the reason is the same: I am with you.
devotion.teens: Joshua inherits a leadership nobody could match, and God's answer to his fear is not a strategy. It is presence. Courage in the Bible is almost never the absence of fear; it is action taken while afraid, on the grounds of who God is.

title: YOU ARE THE LIGHT
text: You are the light of the world. A city located on a hill can’t be hidden. Even so, let your light shine before men, that they may see your good works and glorify your Father who is in heaven.

reflection.kids: A light is not for looking at. It is for helping people see.
reflection.teens: Jesus assumes discipleship is visible — and that the visibility points away from you.

prayer.kids: Jesus, help my life show people something good about you.
prayer.teens: Jesus, keep me from hiding, and from making it about me.

challenge.kids: Say something kind out loud to someone today.
challenge.teens: Do something good today that nobody will thank you for.

devotion.kids: Jesus does not say ‘be a light’. He says you are one. The only question is whether it is under a bucket.
devotion.teens: The image is public by design. Notice where the glory lands in verse 16 — not on the disciple. Visible goodness that draws attention to itself has missed the point of the sentence.

title: DO NOT WORRY
text: Therefore don’t be anxious for tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Each day’s own evil is sufficient.

reflection.kids: Tomorrow has its own stuff. Today is enough for today.
reflection.teens: Jesus does not say worry is wrong. He says it does not work, and he gives you a smaller unit to carry.

prayer.kids: God, I give you the things I am worried about.
prayer.teens: God, here is what I keep rehearsing instead of sleeping. Take it.

challenge.kids: Tell one grown-up you trust about something that worries you.
challenge.teens: Write down the thing you are anxious about, then name one part of it you can actually act on.

devotion.kids: Jesus points at birds and flowers — things that are looked after without worrying about it.
devotion.teens: The argument runs from lesser to greater inside a creation theology: if God sustains what is temporary, the anxiety you carry about your own life is misdirected effort, not realism.

title: LOVE ONE ANOTHER
text: A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another. Just as I have loved you, you also love one another. By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another.

reflection.kids: Jesus gave one new rule: love each other the way he loves you.
reflection.teens: The measure is impossible on purpose, and it is set hours before the cross defines it.

prayer.kids: Jesus, help me love the people around me today.
prayer.teens: Jesus, love through me the person I find hardest.

challenge.kids: Be kind to someone you find annoying.
challenge.teens: Be generous today towards someone who has not earned it from you.

devotion.kids: The world was going to recognise Jesus' friends by one thing — not their music, not their buildings. How they treated each other.
devotion.teens: ‘As I have loved you’ is the clause that makes this new. It is not reciprocity; it is a standard set by someone about to be crucified.

title: ASK, AND IT WILL BE GIVEN
text: Ask, and it will be given you. Seek, and you will find. Knock, and it will be opened for you.

reflection.kids: Keep asking God. He likes it when you talk to him.
reflection.teens: The verbs are continuous: keep asking, keep seeking. Prayer here is a posture, not a transaction.

prayer.kids: God, thank you that I can talk to you about anything.
prayer.teens: God, teach me to keep asking when nothing seems to be happening.

challenge.kids: Pray for someone else today — not for yourself.
challenge.teens: Pray for the same thing every day this week and see what changes in you.

devotion.kids: Jesus says God is like a good parent who wants to give good things.
devotion.teens: The passage argues from lesser to greater: if flawed parents give good gifts, God's character is not stingy. It does not promise a vending machine.

title: I CAN DO ALL THINGS
text: I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me.

reflection.kids: Paul said this when things were hard, not easy.
reflection.teens: Written from prison, about contentment in plenty and in need — not about winning.

prayer.kids: Jesus, give me strength for today.
prayer.teens: Jesus, teach me contentment, not just capability.

challenge.kids: Finish something you started and want to give up on.
challenge.teens: Notice one thing you are treating as unbearable that is actually just uncomfortable.

devotion.kids: This is one of the most quoted verses in the world. It was written by a man in chains.
devotion.teens: Verses 11–12 define ‘all things’ as having plenty and having nothing. Lifting it out of that context turns a verse about sufficiency into a slogan about achievement.

title: THE LORD IS MY SHEPHERD
text: Yahweh is my shepherd; I shall lack nothing. He makes me lie down in green pastures. He leads me beside still waters. He restores my soul.

reflection.kids: A shepherd looks after the sheep all day and all night. God looks after you like that.
reflection.teens: Written by a shepherd about being shepherded — he knew exactly how much work it takes.

prayer.kids: God, thank you for looking after me.
prayer.teens: God, I am not good at being led. Lead me anyway.

challenge.kids: Take five quiet minutes today with no screen.
challenge.teens: Take a walk with no phone and no music, and let it be boring.

devotion.kids: David had been a shepherd. He knew sheep are not clever and still get looked after.
devotion.teens: The psalm turns from ‘he’ to ‘you’ exactly where the valley appears. Grammar carrying theology: in trouble, God stops being spoken about and starts being spoken to.

title: A FRIEND LOVES
text: A friend loves at all times; and a brother is born for adversity.

reflection.kids: A real friend is still your friend when things go wrong.
reflection.teens: The proverb defines friendship by what survives trouble, not by what happens on a good day.

prayer.kids: God, help me be a good friend.
prayer.teens: God, show me who needs me to be steady right now.

challenge.kids: Check on a friend you have not spoken to in a while.
challenge.teens: Turn up for someone this week when it is inconvenient.

devotion.kids: Anyone can be a friend when it is easy. The Bible measures it in the hard times.
devotion.teens: Hebrew wisdom repeatedly tests relationships against adversity. Durability, not intensity, is the standard.
